summary: Adds a new ESM-only `@cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline` subpath (Encryption factory + encrypt/decrypt over WASM protect-ffi and auth AccessKeyStrategy), a Deno CI smoke test and a Supabase Edge example. The riskier part for existing users is not the new subpath but what ships alongside it: the Node entry's native dependency moves protect-ffi 0.23.0 -> 0.24.0 (whose new conditional exports also change which type declarations consumers resolve), `@cipherstash/auth` becomes a stack dependency and moves 0.36.0 -> 0.38.0 for the CLI and wizard, zod and @byteslice/result are now bundled into every stack entry, and stack's version is hand-bumped to 0.18.0 in a changesets repo. All 8 CI checks are green, including Node 22/24, Bun, E2E and the new Deno job, which is the main mitigation for the protect-ffi bump. The new WASM client also diverges from the Node client on null handling (no null short-circuit), which matters once edge and Node code share a table. No plaintext-exposure or wrong-key mechanism was found. Focused review is advised on the protect-ffi/auth bumps and on WASM/Node payload parity.

behaviour_changes.description: New published subpath `./wasm-inline` (ESM import only, no require branch) exporting Encryption(), WasmEncryptionClient (encrypt/decrypt/isEncrypted only, no bulk, query, model or lock-context support), schema builders and isEncrypted. Unlike the Node entry it throws errors rather than returning Result objects, and it requires an explicit region.

The Node/native path of @cipherstash/stack moves from @cipherstash/protect-ffi 0.23.0 to 0.24.0, including all per-platform native binaries. Every existing encrypt/decrypt/query call in the main entry runs on the new native module.

@cipherstash/auth becomes a runtime dependency of stack (catalog 0.38.0). The CLI and wizard, which import the native `@cipherstash/auth` default export for login and token fetching, move from 0.36.0 to 0.38.0. They also gain explicit per-platform auth optionalDependencies.

tsup now runs two configs into a shared dist/ with clean:false (a prebuild script deletes dist instead). zod and @byteslice/result are bundled (noExternal) into all main ESM/CJS entries, not just wasm-inline. tsconfig adds customConditions ['node'] so stack's own declaration build resolves protect-ffi's NAPI types.

packages/stack version is hand-edited from 0.17.0 to 0.18.0, although releases go through changesets (`pnpm run build && changeset publish`) and a pending minor changeset for stack already exists. No changeset is added for the wasm-inline feature, the protect-ffi bump or the cli/wizard auth bump.

New CI job `wasm-e2e-tests` runs on every pull_request with CS_CLIENT_ID/KEY/ACCESS_KEY secrets, builds stack, fails if secrets are missing, and runs a Deno round-trip without FFI permission. @cipherstash/auth* is added to pnpm minimumReleaseAgeExclude.

failure_scenarios.title: protect-ffi 0.24.0 native bump changes payloads or API for existing Node users without a matching EQL bump
failure_scenarios.trigger: An existing stack user upgrades and encrypts/queries against a database with the EQL 2.3.x SQL bundle, or decrypts payloads written by 0.23.0.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Every main-entry operation now runs on protect-ffi 0.24.0 (package.json:217). The repository's own CI comment says postgres-eql 2.3.1 matches the protect-ffi 0.23.x payload format and must be bumped in lockstep (tests.yml:21-22). The image was not bumped. The PR asserts 0.24 is WASM-focused and not a format bump, but the protect-ffi changelog is not available to confirm it.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If 0.24 changed payload shape or search-term encoding, newly written values could fail to index or match in existing databases, or older payloads could fail to decrypt. That is a cross-version compatibility problem affecting data at rest, and npm publication cannot be undone.

existing_verification.description: Run Tests (Node 22/24), Run Tests (Bun) and Run E2E Tests jobs passed on head; the Node job runs against postgres-eql 2.3.1.

missing_verification: No test decrypts or queries a fixture payload written by protect-ffi 0.23.0 (read compatibility with data at rest).
No review of the protect-ffi 0.24.0 changelog or Node API diff is recorded.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Confirm from the protect-ffi 0.24.0 release notes that the Node API and EQL payload/search-term format are unchanged. Add or run a fixture test that decrypts and queries 0.23-written ciphertexts, and update the stale tests.yml lockstep comment.

failure_scenarios.title: WASM client encrypts null into a real ciphertext where the Node client returns null
failure_scenarios.trigger: Edge or Deno code calls client.encrypt(null, ...) for a nullable column, which the WasmPlaintext type explicitly allows, on a table that Node code also reads or queries.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: WasmPlaintext includes null (wasm-inline.ts:108-112), and WasmEncryptionClient.encrypt passes plaintext straight to wasmEncrypt with no null guard (wasm-inline.ts:205-218). The Node operations short-circuit null (encrypt.ts:63, decrypt.ts:51). The pending changeset documents that protect-ffi otherwise turns null into a real SteVec ciphertext.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Rows written from the edge store an encrypted value instead of SQL NULL, so `IS NULL` filters and nullable-field semantics silently diverge between rows written by WASM and rows written by Node. The same app sees different data depending on runtime, and nothing errors.

existing_verification.description: Deno round-trip test covers a non-null string only.

missing_verification: No test of encrypt(null)/decrypt(null) on the wasm-inline client.
No cross-runtime test that WASM-written payloads (including cast_as normalisation by stack's toEqlCastAs rather than protect-ffi's internal normaliser) are identical in shape to Node-written ones.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Mirror the Node null short-circuit in WasmEncryptionClient.encrypt/decrypt, or remove null from WasmPlaintext. Add a parity test that compares WASM and Node payload metadata for each cast_as.

failure_scenarios.title: Consumers' TypeScript resolves protect-ffi WASM types for stack's main-entry declarations
failure_scenarios.trigger: A TypeScript app using moduleResolution 'bundler' (or other resolution without the `node` condition) upgrades to this stack release.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: stack's public types are derived from protect-ffi (types.ts:7-13, `Client = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof newClient>>` at line 29). Stack's own tsconfig needed customConditions ['node'] because under bundler resolution protect-ffi 0.24 otherwise resolves to WASM types with a different newClient signature (tsconfig.json:18-24). That setting fixes stack's build only; consumers resolve the emitted .d.ts with their own conditions.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Consumers may see compile errors or silently different types (Client, Encrypted, JsPlaintext) after a minor upgrade. The failure is mostly loud, at build time, and recoverable by pinning.
missing_verification: No consumer fixture type-checks the packed stack against bundler resolution without customConditions.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a type-check fixture that installs the packed tarball under moduleResolution 'bundler' and 'node16'. Alternatively, import Node types from an unconditional protect-ffi subpath or inline the needed types.

failure_scenarios.title: CLI/wizard auth 0.36 -> 0.38 upgrade breaks login or token fetch
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs `stash auth login`, `stash init` or the wizard after the CLI/wizard are next published with auth 0.38.0.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The catalog moves @cipherstash/auth from 0.36.0 to 0.38.0 (pnpm-workspace.yaml), which cli and wizard consume via catalog:repo. They call the native default export (login.ts, fetch-prompt.ts `const { AutoStrategy } = auth`). These are 0.x minor bumps whose API changes are unknown here. The wizard unit test mocks @cipherstash/auth.
failure_scenarios.consequence: CLI login or wizard prompt fetching fails for users. The failure is loud, but onboarding is blocked until a patched release ships.

existing_verification.description: Run Tests jobs (which include the CLI E2E step) passed; whether they exercise real auth login is not visible.

missing_verification: No evidence of a real-auth login exercise with 0.38.0 on each platform binary.
No changeset or CHANGELOG entry for cli/wizard records the dependency change.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Review the auth 0.37/0.38 changelog for changes to the default export and AutoStrategy, smoke-test `stash auth login`, and add changesets for cli and wizard.

failure_scenarios.title: Hand-edited 0.18.0 version conflicts with changesets release flow
failure_scenarios.trigger: The next release run of `changeset version`/`changeset publish` on main.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/stack/package.json now says 0.18.0 while a pending minor changeset for stack already exists. Changesets would bump from 0.18.0 to 0.19.0, so 0.18.0 may never be published. The wasm-inline feature and protect-ffi bump have no changeset, so the CHANGELOG would not mention them.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Version skips and an incomplete changelog for a release that changes the native dependency. Customers cannot tell from release notes that protect-ffi changed. Low, recoverable impact.
missing_verification: No dry-run of `changeset version` on this branch.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Revert the manual version bump and add changesets for stack (wasm-inline + protect-ffi 0.24), cli and wizard.

verification_gaps.description: No backward-compatibility test reading 0.23-written ciphertexts or querying with 0.24 search terms against existing EQL data. CI integration tests write and read with the same version.
The WASM client is tested only for a single non-null string round-trip; there is no null case and no parity check against Node-written payloads.
No consumer type-check of the packed package under common moduleResolution settings.
Real-auth CLI login against auth 0.38.0 is not shown to be exercised.

recommended_controls.description: Before release, confirm from the protect-ffi 0.24.0 notes that the Node API and payload/search-term format are unchanged. Run a fixture test that decrypts and queries data written by 0.23.0 against EQL 2.3.1.
Add a null short-circuit to the wasm-inline encrypt/decrypt (or drop null from WasmPlaintext) with a unit test. Add a WASM-vs-Node payload-shape parity test covering every cast_as.
Add a packed-tarball consumer type-check (bundler and node16 resolution, skipLibCheck off).
Review the auth 0.36->0.38 changes affecting the default export and AutoStrategy, and smoke-test `stash auth login`.
Replace the manual version bump with changesets for stack, cli and wizard so the release notes record the native dependency change.
